description: Fabric backpressure and how much traffic the host adapters are actually moving. Separates live congestion (counter growth inside the selected range) from lifetime counters that may be historic. Source: ib_hca_port_xmit_wait, ib_hca_out_of_buffer, ib_hca_rnr_nak_retry_err, ib_hca_port_rcv_data, ib_hca_port_xmit_data.

Source: ib_hca_* counters read on every DGX tray by node-exporter, four rails per tray. Every number on the left of a band is backed by the table beside it, built from the identical selector — the table footer prints the row count.

panels.title: Backpressure happening now (counter growth inside the selected range)

panels.description: The adapter had data to send but no credit to send it: the fabric pushed back. Measured as counter growth across the dashboard time range. Source: ib_hca_*, read on every DGX tray by node-exporter. The table beside this number is built from the identical selector, so its row count equals the number shown.
panels.title: Rails accumulating transmit-wait

panels.description: One row per rail whose transmit-wait counter grew inside the range. Row count equals the number on the left.

defaults.noValue: No rail accumulated transmit-wait inside the selected range.

panels.title: Rails accumulating transmit-wait in the range — the exact rails

panels.description: Packets arrived with no receive buffer posted. Usually a slow or stalled consumer on this tray rather than a fabric fault. Source: ib_hca_*, read on every DGX tray by node-exporter. The table beside this number is built from the identical selector, so its row count equals the number shown.
panels.title: Rails hitting receive-buffer exhaustion

panels.description: One row per rail whose out-of-buffer counter grew inside the range. Row count equals the number on the left.

defaults.noValue: No rail exhausted its receive buffers inside the selected range.

panels.title: Rails hitting receive-buffer exhaustion in the range — the exact rails
Backpressure since the adapter last reset

panels.description: Rails whose lifetime transmit-wait counter is non-zero. Lifetime counters include historic backpressure; the range-scoped number in the band above is the actionable one. Source: ib_hca_port_xmit_wait, read on every DGX tray by node-exporter. The table beside this number is built from the identical selector, so its row count equals the number shown.
panels.title: Rails with transmit-wait history

panels.description: One row per rail with a non-zero lifetime counter. Row count equals the number on the left.
panels.title: Rails with transmit-wait history — the exact rails (counter since boot)

panels.description: Receiver-Not-Ready retries: the peer had no buffer and asked the sender to try again. Endemic at low levels on a busy fabric. Source: ib_hca_*, read on every DGX tray by node-exporter. The table beside this number is built from the identical selector, so its row count equals the number shown.
panels.title: Rails with RNR NAK retries

panels.description: One row per rail with a non-zero counter. Row count equals the number on the left.

defaults.noValue: No rail has recorded an RNR NAK retry.

panels.title: Rails with RNR NAK retries — the exact rails (counter since boot)

panels.description: Bytes per second received across all selected rails. IB data counters are in 32-bit words, so the raw rate is multiplied by 4. Rate is measured over a fixed 5-minute window. This is a SUM, so the table beside it sums to this number rather than matching its row count.
